title: llm-prefetch-routing-brainstorm-scratchpad-amelia-chen
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
- Personal scratchpad for prefetch + routing ideas. Trying to capture rough product direction, tradeoffs, and quick user stories before formalizing into a PRD.
- Focus: reduce tail latency and per-token cost by combining proactive KV prefetch (hot-prefix caching) with smarter request routing and inexpensive model fallbacks.

Background / motivation:
- Observed workload: many requests share common prefixes (chat threads with repeated system prompt or context), small % of tokens are hot and reused across requests.
- Current runtime supports KV cache but only on-request; no proactive warming. Routing is simple: cheapest compatible model or region.
- Problem: cold-start KV misses causing 50-200ms tail on many QPS patterns; high-cost when long contexts repeatedly re-compute early layers.

High-level idea(s):
1) Predictive KV prefetch: track prefix popularity per route/model, proactively compute and warm KV cache for top-N prefixes on each serving node/pool during idle windows.
   - lightweight predictor using recent sliding window counts + exponential decay.
   - TTL and eviction based on recency/size budget per node.
   - Option: cooperative caching metadata placed in routing layer to avoid duplicate prefetch across nodes.

2) Routing-aware prefetch triggers: when routing decision picks a model variant for a request, route-level analytics can decide to trigger prefetch for sibling prefixes (e.g., user starts typing -> prefetch likely next tokens).

3) Cheap-fallback speculative decoding: for long inputs, try a narrow-quantized model to precompute early layers (or first K layers) then stitch with full model if needed. Prefetch + fallback combined for cost savings.

User stories / acceptance criteria (rough):
- As an SRE, I want tail p95 latency for chat completions to drop by at least 20% for customers with >1000 QPS, without increasing overall GPU hours by >10%.
- As a platform engineer, I want controls to configure per-pool prefetch budgets (memory, allowed CPU background windows) and ability to opt-out on customer routes with sensitive data.
- As a product owner, I want telemetry showing hit-rate uplift (prefetch hit vs baseline), cost delta, and failed-stitch events.

Implementation sketch / components:
- Prefetch predictor service (lightweight in runtime agent or separate microservice?) stores top prefixes per route, exports small bloom/hash lists to serving nodes.
- Serving node prefetch worker: background job that pulls list, executes forward pass up to layer K (or full KV generation) and writes KV to node-local cache. Must respect GPU scheduling windows.
- Routing metadata extension: add prefix popularity signals to routing decisions; if a route is chosen, inform node to prefetch sibling prefixes.
- Config surface in console: per-customer route toggle, budget sliders, model compatibility matrix.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost model: background prefetch consumes GPU cycles — need guardrails (idle windows, server-side quotas). How to attribute cost to customer? charge as prefetch tokens?
- Privacy/regulatory: prefetching could expose sensitive prefixes or customer data to other nodes or logs. Need strict isolation and KMS policies. Option: restrict prefetch to private deployments only initially.
- Correctness: stitching cached KV from quantized/cheap model to full model — risk of mismatched hidden states. Might need standard interface/constraints (only prefetch up to layer L where representations compatible).
- Distribution: how to avoid duplicated prefetch across many nodes? Cooperative protocol or central coordinator? Tradeoff with complexity.

Quick metrics to track (proto):
- Prefetch hit rate per route (hits / attempted requests)
- p50/p95 latency delta vs baseline (prefetch off)
- GPU prefetch utilization (GPU-seconds / walltime)
- Cost per saved token ($) estimate
- Failed stitches / mismatch rate

Experiment plan (alpha):
- Stage 0: offline simulation using request traces + sampled model runs to estimate candidate prefixes and costs.
- Stage 1: Small-scale canary in Hosted API with non-sensitive public dataset routes (10% traffic of selected routes). Measure hit-rate, latency.
- Stage 2: Expand to dedicated pools where we can reserve GPU background windows. Add opt-in in Console.

MVP scope (what to build first):
- Minimal predictor (LR/decay counts) + node-local prefetch worker that computes full KV for top prefixes, conservative budget (1-2% GPU spare). No fancy routing integration.
- Telemetry: expose prefetch hits and latencies in Console per-route.
- Safety: per-customer opt-out, default off.

Nice-to-have / future:
- Cross-node cooperative caching (bloom exchange), smarter ML predictor for next-token/prefix forecasting, compatibility with quantized fallback stitching.
- Automatic budget tuning: link to Redwood Optimize to recommend budgets based on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Notes / todo (me):
- Talk to Noah about compatibility/stitching constraints (noah.k@redwood) — what layers can be safely precomputed?
- Check ENG-4821 for earlier prefetch experiments and simulation traces.
- Draft quick telemetry schema and add to Console backlog.
- Add security checklist for prefetch (isolation, logging, retention).

References / links:
- ENG-4821 (prefetch spike experiment)
- convo: #serving-runtime thread T12345 (discussion about KV eviction)
summary: Personal brainstorm scratchpad capturing ideas for combining KV prefetch with routing and cheap model fallbacks to reduce tail latency and cost. Contains user stories, implementation notes, open questions, and an experiment plan.
